title: U.S. House · Kansas's 1st District
area: Western and central Kansas, including Garden City, Salina, Hays and Manhattan ("Big First")

context.text: Incumbent Tracey Mann (R) defeated Craig Musser in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary. Lauren Reinhold defeated Colin McRoberts in the Democratic primary. The district's 2026 Cook Partisan Voter Index is R+16.

summary.text: Tracey Mann is the Republican incumbent representing Kansas's 1st District, first elected in 2020 and seeking a fourth term. A fifth-generation Kansan from a family farm near Quinter, he worked in commercial real estate and briefly served as Lieutenant Governor of Kansas in 2018-2019 before entering Congress. He serves on the House Agriculture and Transportation and Infrastructure committees and chairs the Agriculture Committee's Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry subcommittee.

background.text: Born in 1976 in Quinter, Kansas. According to his official biography, he is a fifth-generation Kansan who was born and raised on his family's farm south of Quinter and spent time working in the family's fields and feed yard.
Earned a bachelor's degree in agricultural economics from Kansas State University in 2000.
Worked in commercial real estate and served on the loan committee of First National Bank Syracuse, according to his official biography.
Served on the boards of Kansas Agriculture and Rural Leadership, the Kansas Chamber of Commerce, the City Teen Center in Salina, and Legacy Financial.

Was appointed Lieutenant Governor of Kansas in 2018 by Governor Jeff Colyer, who became governor after Sam Brownback was appointed to a post in the Trump administration. Ballotpedia lists his term as 2018-2019.
Ran in the August 2018 Republican primary for Lieutenant Governor of Kansas, finishing second to Wink Hartman, 40.5% to 40.6%.

Won the Republican primary for the open 1st District seat in August 2020, defeating Bill Clifford, Jerry Molstad, and Michael Soetaert, and won the November 2020 general election, succeeding Roger Marshall, who was elected to the U.S. Senate. He was re-elected in 2022 and 2024 and won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary over Craig Musser.
Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture, where he chairs the Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry Subcommittee, and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (2025-2026 assignments).
According to his official biography, lives in Salina, Kansas, with his wife Audrey and their four children.

candidates.name: Lauren Reinhold

summary.text: Lauren Reinhold is the Democratic nominee for Kansas's 1st District and a Lawrence-based attorney. Describes herself as having nearly 30 years of public-service legal and administrative work, including as a Legal Aid and immigration attorney, union leader, and federal administrator; according to the Kansas Reflector, her Social Security Administration position was eliminated in 2025 and she decided to run afterward. She won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary and is running on affordability, health care, and workers' rights.

background.text: Born in Missouri and, according to her Ballotpedia survey, spent most of her life in Kansas as her parents, both public servants, moved between the two states. The Kansas Reflector reports she was raised in Topeka, Kansas City, and St. Louis.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Northeast Missouri State University in 1992 and a law degree from the University of Kansas School of Law in 1996.
Began her legal career in 1996. Before her federal roles, she specialized in immigration law in private practice, according to the Kansas Reflector.

Describes nearly 30 years of public service as a Legal Aid attorney, immigration attorney, disability advocate, union leader, and federal government administrator, including 16 years of federal experience.

Worked for several years at the U.S. Social Security Administration in Kansas, first as an attorney and then as a human resources administrator, until the position was eliminated in 2025 during Department of Government Efficiency cuts; she also served two years as an officer in her federal employee union chapter.
Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary for the 1st District over Colin McRoberts, 64.2% to 35.8% per Ballotpedia.

priorities.text: Wants every job to pay enough to cover housing, health care, childcare, transportation and education, with money left to save.

Calls for tax reform so wealthy people "pay their share," affordable and accessible health care for all, a path to citizenship for hardworking immigrant residents, and a steep increase to the minimum wage.
Says the federal government should serve the public rather than corporations and the wealthy, and says she opposes the Project 2025 plan and DOGE's reduction of federal agencies.

positions.quote: a steep increase to the minimum wage, as a start

candidates.name: Steven Jacob

summary.text: Steven Jacob is the Libertarian candidate for Kansas's 1st District. He describes himself as a 55-year-old retiree and is running on reducing federal spending and the national debt and ending U.S. involvement in foreign wars. Little other biographical information is publicly available.

background.text: Graduated from Lawrence High School, according to Ballotpedia.
Describes himself as a 55-year-old retiree who says both parties spend without limit. Ballotpedia lists his profession as retired.

priorities.text: Opposes continued federal deficit spending, saying both major parties spend without addressing inflation and are passing debt to future generations.
Calls for ending U.S. involvement in wars abroad, including funding he says supports conflict in the Middle East.

candidates.researchNotes: Limited public record found; based only on his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response.

Key floor votes and FEC finance totals for incumbent Tracey Mann are added separately by script.
